primary.title: Cyclone Murasu tracker: Where is the storm?
primary.description: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu is moving closer to the south Andhra Pradesh coast, with landfall expected between Nellore and Narsapur, near Ongole, during the early hours of Tuesday, November 3. The storm is likely to bring strong winds of 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph. As Andhra Pradesh prepares for the cyclone, neighbouring Tamil Nadu has sent 500 electricity department personnel to help restore power supply disrupted by the storm. Three National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams, comprising 90 personnel, have also been deployed from Tamil Nadu to assist with rescue and relief operations.Also Read: Weather today, November 2: IMD warns of heavy rain in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu; Delhi-NCR's AQI becomes 'severe'; check latest IMD update and AQI levels— Indiametdept (@Indiametdept) Cyclone Murasu tracker: Latest storm position and movementAccording to the India Meteorological Department's (IMD) bulletin issued at 8.30 pm on November 2, Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu moved north-northwestwards at a speed of 12 kmph over the west-central Bay of Bengal during the preceding six hours. The storm was centred near latitude 14.9°N and longitude 80.6°E, off the south Andhra Pradesh coast. It was located around 60 km east of Kavali, 80 km northeast of Nellore, 90 km southeast of Ongole and 160 km south-southwest of Machilipatnam.The weather department said Murasu was likely to continue moving northwestwards before crossing the south Andhra Pradesh coast.Cyclone Murasu landfall: IMD predicts winds up to 120 kmphThe IMD has forecast that Murasu will cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast as a severe cyclonic storm between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole. Wind speeds are likely to remain between 100 and 110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph during the crossing. The cyclone is being continuously monitored by Doppler Weather Radars located in Chennai, Machilipatnam and Visakhapatnam.Tamil Nadu sends 500 electricity personnel to Andhra PradeshTamil Nadu has organised 25 teams of electricity department personnel, totalling 500 workers, to help Andhra Pradesh restore power supply disrupted by the cyclone.Electricity Minister R Nirmal Kumar said the deployment followed a request from Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu. The teams will assist the neighbouring state with electricity restoration work as it prepares for the impact of Murasu.Three NDRF teams deployed for rescue and relief operationsThree NDRF teams, comprising 90 personnel, have been sent from the force's 4th Battalion near Arakkonam in Tamil Nadu to support disaster management efforts in Andhra Pradesh.Each team has 30 personnel and is being deployed to areas including Nellore, Prakasam and Markapuram. The teams will assist with rescue operations, debris clearance and relief work in areas affected by the cyclone.Cyclone Murasu: Heavy rainfall warning for OdishaThe southern districts of Odisha are also likely to receive heavy rainfall as Murasu affects weather conditions along the east coast. The IMD has forecast rainfall of 7 cm to 20 cm on November 2 and 3. Parts of the state may also experience winds of 50-60 kmph, with gusts reaching 70 kmph, on November 3.The NDRF and Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) have been kept on standby in vulnerable areas. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea between November 2 and 4.In Ganjam district, officials have been directed to stock essential supplies and shift residents from high-risk areas to designated shelters as part of cyclone preparedness measures.
